transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Redbridge University. My name is Amara Singh, and I'm the head of student services. I know that the first week can feel overwhelming, so I'd like to explain a few things that will make your life easier.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: First, registration. You should all have received an email with a link to the online system. Most of you have already completed it, but about thirty students still haven't confirmed their course choices. If that's you, please do it by Friday. After that date, there's a late fee of twenty-five pounds, which I'd rather you didn't have to pay.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Second, the library. It was recently refurbished and now has three floors. The ground floor is for group work, and talking is fine there. The first floor is for quiet study, and the second floor, which used to be open to everyone, is now silent study only. Some of you might think that's strict, but exam time is very busy, and students told us they needed a place with absolutely no noise. Your student card opens the doors, and you can borrow up to fifteen books at a time. The library is open until midnight on weekdays, but originally we planned to close at ten, so you can thank last year's student union for changing that.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Third, accommodation. Those living in halls will find the laundry in the basement of each building. Please don't leave your clothes in the machines for hours, because other students are waiting. If you live off campus, the number fourteen bus runs every ten minutes from the city centre, and your student card gives you a thirty per cent discount.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Fourth, support services. If you ever feel stressed or worried, you aren't alone. Many students do at some point. The counselling service is free and confidential, and you don't need a doctor's letter to use it. You can book an appointment online, or just walk in between two and four every afternoon. Also, the writing centre helps with essays. A lot of first-year students think the centre is only for people who are weak at writing, but that isn't true. In fact, some of our best students go there before every assignment.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Finally, I'd like to encourage you to join a society. There are over a hundred, from chess to climbing. The societies fair takes place next Wednesday in the main hall, so don't miss it. Joining one is the quickest way to make friends who are outside your course. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your first week.
